Then report each step's result.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). availableCommands.name: ai-gateway
availableCommands.description: AI Gateway exposes models from multiple providers through shared authentication, model IDs, routing, billing, and observability. Model availability, SDK APIs, CLI commands, prices, and product capabilities change frequently. Verify them from current sources before changing code.

availableCommands.name: ai-sdk
availableCommands.description: The AI SDK by Vercel (the ai package on npm) is a TypeScript toolkit for building AI applications. It provides a unified API across model providers for text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, embeddings, and framework UI integrations.

availableCommands.name: upstream
availableCommands.description: Answer questions about the AI SDK and help build AI-powered features. Use when developers: (1) Ask about AI SDK functions like generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, or tools, (2) Want to build AI agents, chatbots, RAG systems, or text generation features, (3) Have questions about AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.), streaming, tool calling, structured output, or embeddings, (4) Use React hooks like useChat or useCompletion. Triggers on: "AI SDK", "Vercel AI SDK", "generateText", "streamText", "add AI to my app", "build an agent", "tool calling", "structured output", "useChat".

availableCommands.name: auth
availableCommands.description: You are an expert in authentication for Vercel-deployed applications — covering Clerk (native Vercel Marketplace integration), Better Auth (self-hosted, with data in your own database), Descope, and Auth0 for application sign-in, plus Vercel's own primitives: Sign in with Vercel (OAuth/OIDC provider), Passport (deployment protection with your identity provider), and KMS (managed signing keys).

availableCommands.name: bootstrap
availableCommands.description: Project bootstrapping orchestrator for repos that depend on Vercel-linked resources (databases, auth, and managed integrations). Use when setting up or repairing a repository so linking, environment provisioning, env pulls, and first-run db/dev commands happen in the correct safe order.

availableCommands.name: botid
availableCommands.description: Protect specific routes and server actions from bots in code with Vercel BotID (`botid` npm package). Use when installing BotID, calling `initBotId()` or `checkBotId()`, mounting `<BotIdClient />`, gating signup, login, checkout or AI inference endpoints, allowing verified bots such as ChatGPT agents through, enabling Deep Analysis, or debugging a route that always reports a bot. For site-wide bot rules (Bot Protection, AI Bots, custom rules on bot name or category), use the `vercel-firewall` skill.

availableCommands.name: build-agents
availableCommands.description: Default guidance for building AI agents. Use for generic requests to build, create, scaffold, design, architect, or implement an AI agent, agent app, tool-calling agent, durable agent, multi-agent system, or scheduled agent.

availableCommands.name: cdn-caching
availableCommands.description: Debug Vercel CDN caching — cache hit rate, stale content, revalidation behavior, ISR + PPR, per-request cache reasons (cacheReason) and PPR state (ppr_state), and costs.

availableCommands.name: chat-sdk
availableCommands.description: Unified TypeScript SDK for building chat bots across Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Discord, Telegram, GitHub, Linear, WhatsApp, and more. Write your bot logic once, deploy everywhere.

availableCommands.name: client-side-security
availableCommands.description: Protect what runs in your users' browsers on Vercel with a Content-Security-Policy header and Page Integrity script monitoring. Use when adding or debugging a CSP, choosing where to set it (Next.js proxy.ts or next.config.js, vercel.json, Project Routes), allowing Vercel Toolbar under CSP, monitoring third-party scripts or tag managers, or meeting PCI DSS script requirements. For WAF rules and rate limits use `vercel-firewall`; for bots use `botid`.

availableCommands.name: create-a-backend
availableCommands.description: Backend architecture guidance. Use when planning, building, or migrating an API or backend; choosing between Functions, Services, containers, Daemons, Workflow, Queues, and Marketplace databases; or selecting a supported backend framework or runtime.

availableCommands.name: custom-metrics
availableCommands.description: Emit and query Vercel Custom Metrics. Use proactively whenever you write or change server code that runs as a Vercel Function (route handlers, API routes, server actions, webhooks, scheduled jobs, queue consumers, AI or external API calls) to record outcomes and latency with metric() from @vercel/functions, even when the user did not ask for metrics. Also use when choosing metric names and attributes or querying emitted values with vc metrics.

availableCommands.name: daemons
availableCommands.description: Vercel Daemons guidance — long-running background workers built from a Dockerfile and declared under the `daemons` key in vercel.json. Use when running queue consumers, Celery/Sidekiq/BullMQ workers, workflow workers, or job runners next to an app on Vercel; configuring daemon instances per region, memory, or command; handling SIGTERM; or choosing between Daemons, Functions, Queues, and Workflows.

availableCommands.name: deployments-cicd
availableCommands.description: Vercel deployment and CI/CD expert guidance. Use when deploying, promoting, rolling back, inspecting deployments, building with --prebuilt, or configuring CI workflow files for Vercel.

availableCommands.name: domains
availableCommands.description: Search, register, connect, transfer, and renew domain names on Vercel using the CLI or Domains Registrar API. Use for domain availability and pricing, custom domains, DNS records, nameservers, ownership verification, and domain orders.

availableCommands.name: env-vars
availableCommands.description: Vercel environment variable expert guidance. Use when working with .env files, vercel env commands, Secret or Config variable types, OIDC tokens, or managing environment-specific configuration.

availableCommands.name: eve
availableCommands.description: eve is a filesystem-first framework for durable backend AI agents. An agent is a directory on disk — instructions, skills, tools, connections, channels, subagents, and schedules are all files — and eve compiles and runs it.

availableCommands.name: flags-sdk
availableCommands.description: Implement feature flags in Next.js or SvelteKit code with the Flags SDK (`flags` npm package). Use when installing or configuring the SDK, declaring flags with `flag()`, reading a connected same-team project's flags through Project Connections (`createVercelAdapter({ projectId })`), wiring a provider adapter (`@flags-sdk/vercel`, Statsig, LaunchDarkly, PostHog, GrowthBook, Global Config, OpenFeature, and others), using `identify`, `dedupe`, or `evaluate`, keeping pages static with precompute, setting up Flags Explorer, or encrypting flag values. For planning a flag, Vercel Flags rollouts and experiments, the `vercel flags` CLI, or other frameworks, use the `vercel-flags` skill.

availableCommands.name: is-agentic
availableCommands.description: Score how ready a website, domain, or public MCP endpoint is for AI agents using Is Agentic, and read or act on the resulting report. Use when asked to check a site's agent readiness, get its Is Agentic score, fetch a scored report as JSON, or fix the issues that lower a site's score.

availableCommands.name: knowledge-update
availableCommands.description: Corrects outdated LLM knowledge about the Vercel platform and introduces new products. Injected at session start.

availableCommands.name: vercel:marketplace
availableCommands.description: Vercel Marketplace expert guidance — discovering, installing, and managing third-party integrations via the `vercel integration` CLI. Use when building any app that needs an external capability without a dedicated skill — commerce (stores, storefronts, selling products), payments (checkout, subscriptions, billing), observability/monitoring, messaging/email, search, or CMS — or when discovering, installing, or managing integrations.

availableCommands.name: microfrontends
availableCommands.description: Guide for building, configuring, and deploying microfrontends on Vercel. Use this skill when the user mentions microfrontends, multi-zones, splitting an app across teams, independent deployments, cross-app routing, incremental migration, composing multiple frontends under one domain, microfrontends.json, @vercel/microfrontends, the microfrontends local proxy, or path-based routing between Vercel projects. Also use when the user asks about shared layouts across projects, navigation between microfrontends, fallback environments, asset prefixes, or feature flag controlled routing.

availableCommands.name: offload-to-sandbox
availableCommands.description: Offload heavy builds, full test suites and parallel experiments from the local machine to Vercel Sandboxes with the `vercel sandbox` CLI. Use when a local machine is overloaded or shared by several agents, when a test suite should be sharded, or when many tasks should run side by side without consuming local CPU, memory or disk.

availableCommands.name: queues
availableCommands.description: Vercel Queues guidance — durable topics with at-least-once delivery, independent consumer groups, retries, delays, and idempotency keys via @vercel/queue (JS) or vercel-queue (Python). Use when deferring background work, buffering traffic, fanning out events, or choosing between Queues and Workflows.
